answer: Random audit slot lottery. At registration close, an atlas of IDs is frozen; a public VRF beacon then publishes a seed the attacker cannot precompute. Beacon outputs are anchored in a public reef of timestamped hashes. Each pulse assigns a small random audit set to submit ID-bound compute proofs before deadline. A failed proof freezes that ID and its payout. Because assignments are unknown in advance, a sybil operator must keep every identity audit-ready, paying per-ID compute and availability cost each pulse.
